neutral-200.displayName: Gray 200 (FAQ question, ghost label, focus ring)

display.purpose: The hero h1 only, centred, max-w-5xl, balanced.

headline.purpose: Every section h2 via the kit's Heading.

accent.purpose: The one Em phrase per heading; inherits the heading's size.

lead.purpose: Intro under a heading; hero subhead at ~50ch.

body-sm.purpose: Dense body, FAQ answers (68ch), feature lists, pill labels.

meta.purpose: Terms, captions, nav, marquee chips, row labels.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked data keys inside product surfaces only; the smallest size.

data.purpose: Counts, prices in comparisons, handles, pacing stats; tabular numerals.

shadows.name: bezel-highlight
shadows.purpose: Top edge of every panel and dashboard card; travels with the 1px gradient bezel (CARD_BEZEL).

shadows.name: bezel-edge
shadows.purpose: The 1px gradient border, painted on a p-[1px] wrapper.

shadows.name: bezel-edge-accent
shadows.purpose: The lit edge of the card you act in (pricing, approval card).

shadows.name: action-glow
shadows.purpose: Under the white primary pill and auth submit only.

shadows.name: floating-header
shadows.purpose: The condensed header pill, with backdrop-filter: blur(16px) over surface at 70%.

shadows.name: nav-active-inset
shadows.purpose: The scroll-spied section link lifted out of its track.

shadows.name: approve-ready
shadows.purpose: One pulse on the Approve control when the approval card's trace completes.

shadows.name: stage-tab-inset
shadows.purpose: The active Approval Queue stage tab, lifted out of its recessed track onto surface.

shadows.name: after-send-ring
shadows.purpose: The global keyboard ring from index.css, drawn on the Inbox's Next / Close pill that takes focus from script after a send; Chrome does not count Ctrl+Enter as keyboard use, so :focus-visible alone would hide it.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The system's one easing: entrances, pill disc travel, header condense, sheet, FAQ rows, trace underline.

motion.name: ease-in-out-trace
motion.purpose: The highlighter sweep in the approval card (520ms).

motion.name: landing-in
motion.value: 1000ms ease-out-expo; from opacity 0, translateY(28px), blur(8px); delays 0/100/200/260ms
motion.purpose: Hero text entrance, CSS-only, visible by default.

motion.name: control-slow
motion.purpose: PillButton disc travel and padding swap, header condense, sheet slide, FAQ expand.

motion.name: control-fast
motion.purpose: Ghost pill, nav link colour, sheet scrim fade.

motion.name: marquee
motion.value: 45s linear infinite; pauses on hover and offscreen

motion.name: dm-rise
motion.value: 55s linear infinite per column; 9s approval flash

motion.name: hero-canvas
motion.value: requestAnimationFrame, always scheduled; draws only while in view; DPR capped at 2; dt clamped to 48ms
motion.purpose: Variant A magnet field and C radar sweep.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: 400ms opacity fade; canvases render still frames; marquee and DM wall stand still

motion.name: queue-settle
motion.value: 220ms ease-out-expo; from opacity 0.45, translateY(-3px); off under reduced motion
motion.purpose: A dashboard state change settling in place: a newly keyed next-decision band, a row's new state label, the delete strip.

motion.name: inbox-row-settle
motion.value: queue-settle keyframes run through the Web Animations API on the <li>: 220ms ease-out-expo, from opacity 0.45, translateY(-3px); skipped under reduced motion
motion.purpose: An Inbox row that lands in a new place after a new message (folded) or on folding after one. An open row is pinned and never moves.

motion.name: inbox-open-scroll
motion.value: md+: scrollBy just enough to show the composer bottom + 16px (or up to clear the 32px sticky header); below md: row header to the top under the sticky header; smooth, instant under reduced motion
motion.purpose: Opening a conversation brings the work into view.

motion.name: disclosure-turn
motion.purpose: The Inbox row chevron turning 180° and the Autopilot switch knob travelling 14px.

narrative.overview:
MagnetEngine looks like the dashboard it sells. The public pages (`/`, `/lp/b`, `/lp/c`), sign-in, activation, not-found and the extension popup all wear the client dashboard's palette: untinted near-black grounds, white for the one thing to do, grays for everything that is chrome, and green only where something went well. The owner chose the category standard (Linear's hairline precision and dark density, Framer's motion-led first viewport) and asked for it at full fidelity, so the system has no quirks. What makes it this product is what it refuses to fake: no logo strip, avatar stack, star rating or testimonial. Where the reference layout had those, the build shows true material instead: a seat count drawn as the hundred seats it counts, a marquee of niches the product can search, and the approval card itself as live DOM.

Density follows reading, not decoration. A landing section is one heading with one serif-italic phrase, a measured column (`max-w-2xl` to `max-w-3xl` for argument, `max-w-6xl` for the pipeline and header), and hairline-ruled rows instead of card grids. Motion has one job per surface: the hero field dramatises the variant's angle behind the headline, and the approval card plays the product's own mechanism once. Everything else only responds to input.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black grounds with no hue; depth comes from four surface steps and 1px white hairlines, not shadows.
White is the action colour. Emerald (`positive`) and red (`danger`) are the only hues, and each always means something.
One typeface (Schibsted Grotesk) for everything, one Instrument Serif italic phrase per heading, Sometype Mono only for numbers and handles.
Every control is a pill; panels are 1.25rem bezelled rectangles; dashboard cards are 1.5rem.
A continuous hero field behind a legibility scrim, a CSS blur-rise entrance, and a resting state that is always the finished frame.
The proof shown is only proof that exists.

rules.name: The Two Hues Rule
rules.body: Green and red are the only colours in the product, and each must mean something. Green is a good outcome or the confirming half of a pair of actions. Red is destruction or failure. Decoration never earns either. `brand` (orange) is retired from every routed surface. `info`, `accent` and `caution` stay defined, but nothing public or in the dashboard renders them.

rules.name: The Untinted Black Rule
rules.body: The four grounds carry no hue. A black that is not black is a second accent nobody declared.

rules.name: The White Means Act Rule
rules.body: A solid white fill on a control marks the primary action: start the trial or submit the form. The second action is always the hairline ghost pill, never another white pill.

rules.name: The One Italic Phrase Rule
rules.body: A heading may carry one Instrument Serif italic phrase, set through `Em`, and no more. The serif never appears in body copy, UI or data.

rules.name: The Mono Is Measurement Rule
rules.body: Sometype Mono is for numbers, handles and counts, where tabular alignment helps a reader. It is never a way to look technical.

rules.name: The Five Roles Rule
rules.body: Running text uses the five named sizes (`label`, `meta`, `body-sm`, `body`, `lead`). Headings are fluid `clamp()`s set at the call site. Nothing is smaller than `label`.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px white lines at 8% (12% for emphasis), never with drop shadows on cards.

rules.name: The Bezel Travels Together Rule
rules.body: The gradient edge and the inner highlight are one device. Apply them from `CARD_BEZEL`, `CARD_BEZEL_STRONG` or `CARD_BEZEL_DANGER` in `src/lib/theme.ts`, never re-typed inline.

rules.name: The No Card In A Card Rule
rules.body: Inside a dashboard card, groups are ruled with hairlines on the card's own ground, never boxed in a second bezel. The Inbox's three suggested replies are columns divided by 8% rules, not three cards.

rules.name: The Lit Is Not Hover Rule
rules.body: An unread row's ground is its own step (white at 6%), never the value a resting row reaches on hover (3%); lit rows hover one step further (8%). A row that looks hovered must never be mistaken for one that has news.

dos: **Do** take every colour from a token: a Tailwind role class, `theme()` in CSS, or `SURFACE`/`CHANNEL`/`alpha()` from `src/lib/theme.ts` for canvas and inline styles.
**Do** keep one white pill per action group and pair it with a hairline ghost pill for the second action.
**Do** give every heading at most one `Em` phrase in Instrument Serif italic.
**Do** set numbers, handles and prices in Sometype Mono with tabular numerals.
**Do** rule lists with `hairline` rows instead of wrapping each item in a card.
**Do** make every entrance CSS-only and visible by default: `landing-in` (1000ms, 28px rise out of an 8px blur, staggered 0, 100, 200 and 260ms), and a 400ms fade under reduced motion.
**Do** keep hero canvas loops always scheduled, skip drawing while out of view, and render still frames under reduced motion.
**Do** put a scrim behind any text that sits over a motion field, and fade the field before content rises over it.
**Do** print the trial terms (card required, cancel before day 4, the monthly price) wherever the trial is offered.
**Do** set `[color-scheme:dark]` on a product root that holds native form controls (checkboxes, selects, number fields), so the browser draws them dark.
**Do** confirm a bulk or irreversible dashboard action in an inline confirmation strip under the control that asked, and let a changed row keep its place with an Undo rather than leave the table.
**Do** pin an open dashboard row where it opened, and let a row that moves while folded settle into its new place with `queue-settle` rather than reshuffle silently.
**Do** give a control that takes focus from script (the Next pill after a send) the global ring on plain `:focus`, not only `:focus-visible`.
donts: **Don't** use `brand` orange on any routed surface, and don't render `info`, `accent` or `caution` on public pages or in the dashboard.
**Don't** use green or red decoratively. A green point, check, ring or chip must stand for approved, replied, found, captured or free.
**Don't** show logos, avatar stacks, star ratings, testimonials or result numbers the product cannot stand behind. Show seats, terms, searchable niches and the product itself.
**Don't** put an uppercase tracked label above a section heading. The 11px uppercase label is for data keys inside product surfaces.
**Don't** use `neutral-600` or `neutral-700` for text; they are for borders, dividers and disabled chrome.
**Don't** add drop shadows to cards or panels; depth is the bezel and the surface step.
**Don't** gate a hero animation on `document.hidden` or `visibilitychange`.
**Don't** set the serif outside a heading's accent phrase, or the mono outside data.
**Don't** square off a public control; buttons, chips and nav are pills.
**Don't** put a white pill in a destructive confirmation; the confirming control is the red danger pill, and focus starts on Cancel.
**Don't** box items inside a dashboard card in cards of their own; rule them with hairlines on the card's ground.
**Don't** give an unread row the same ground a resting row reaches on hover.
